blocks.text: The second supply theme covers what visitors find once they arrive: product beyond the icons, the quality of the stay and the limits of the flagship sites. The three focus areas work as a set. New product gives visitors a reason to travel outward, quality standards make that product safe to sell and flow management at the flagships sends the overflow to it.

The growth case needs visitors to travel beyond the Cape Peninsula, stay longer and spend in more places. The province has the assets to support that. Of 50,332 mapped tourism assets, the Cape Metro holds 40.3% and the five other districts the rest (Infrastructure Report, Jul 2026, p2, p23). The West Coast has the highest natural-asset attractiveness in the province and the Central Karoo its most unique niche assets (Infrastructure Report, Jul 2026, p88).

Yet both score lowest on readiness, and the product around the assets is unfinished (section 2.3). Eleven of 16 organisations engaged see the offer as concentrated around Cape Town and a narrow set of icons (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p11; the count is reconstructed from the appendix tables). The Department of Economic Development adds that destination development has focused more on managing barriers than on building product outside the Cape Peninsula (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p24).

Concentration costs the province twice. The flagships run full in season while Cape Point and the township attractions are underused (Infrastructure Report, Jul 2026, p24). Further out, strong product sits where visitors cannot easily reach or afford it (Infrastructure Report, Jul 2026, p89).

The evidence locates the constraint. It is less about creating new attractions and more about turning existing assets into complete, accessible visitor experiences (Infrastructure Report, Jul 2026, p114). Each route falls short on something different: accommodation and bookability on the West Coast, bookability on Route 62 and depth beyond Hermanus on the Whale Coast (Infrastructure Report, Jul 2026, p62, p73, p84). The Winelands and the Garden Route fall short only on safety (section 2.3).

No committed capital yet follows the gap (Infrastructure Report, Jul 2026, p54, p76). No source counts the assets that have no product around them [assets with no bookable product or guided access, by district: needs the Wesgro supply database behind the 50,332 count]. The first design task is therefore to size the gap district by district.

Wesgro works outward from strength. The Garden Route, the Cape Winelands and the Overberg already have strong underlying product and need connectivity, packaging and service depth (Infrastructure Report, Jul 2026, p114). Route 62 and the West Coast are packaged as slow-travel products. In 2027 and 2028 the Tourism unit designs bookable itineraries for all six touring routes. Delivery starts from 2029 on the Garden Route, the Cape Winelands and the Overberg, which are closest to ready. It moves to Route 62 and the West Coast once their product is online (focus area 3; section 4.3).

Stellenbosch and George can anchor regional business events, which gives the Convention Bureau a part to play (Demand-Side Analysis, Jun 2026, p41). The capital sits with others. Accommodation investors and municipalities add beds and service depth in secondary towns later in the period (focus area 15). SANParks carries the precinct projects, and rural broadband sits with national government (focus area 3).

rows: Package bookable multi-day itineraries on each of the six touring routes, starting with the Whale Coast east of Hermanus, Route 62 and the West Coast
Activate cold-zone assets with guided tours, interpretation and bookable product, beginning with the marine and wildflower assets
Build regional conference offers in Stellenbosch and George, with stays before and after Cape Town events
Invest in accommodation and service depth beyond Hermanus, in Route 62's secondary towns and beyond Langebaan and Paternoster (focus area 15)
Refresh flagship product: Robben Island beyond the prison tour; the Cableway's lower station
Robben Island Museum; Table Mountain Aerial Cableway
Complete SANParks precinct projects such as the R81.7m Agulhas lighthouse precinct

blocks.text: The actions supply what the assets lack: a guide, a bed and a booking route. Packaging turns scattered assets into a trip a visitor can buy, and a multi-day itinerary gives a reason to stay outside the Metro. The Overberg shows both the pull and the limit. Its whale-watching anchor sustains operator confidence despite flat accessibility, yet De Hoop still lacks accommodation investment and year-round product is unfunded (Infrastructure Report, Jul 2026, p75, p76).

Chile ran Santiago, Valparaíso, the wine valleys and Patagonia as one portfolio. It reports longer stays and shoulder-season revenue from the approach, though no figure is printed for either (Global Benchmarking Report, Mar 2026, p27). The change for the Western Cape is to sell experiences as curated journeys and move from asset marketing to experience-led packaging (Global Benchmarking Report, Mar 2026, p28). The condition is that the other entries keep pace. Itineraries sell only if the product can be booked (focus area 3), reached without a car (focus area 9) and stayed in. Without beds, a packaged route stays a day trip from Cape Town.
